title: Causality Implies the Lorentz Group
relevance: Context for the repaired cone census (RESULT.md section 3.3): Zeeman's causality partial order and his theorem identify the causal-order automorphism group in dimensions >= 3; Remark 2 documents that in 1 space dimension the causality group is much larger. NOT a premise of the repaired census, which uses only the displayed subgroup (translations, orthochronous boosts, dilations, reflection) verified preserving << by direct computation
limits: First page read from the publicly posted PDF (abstract, theorem statement, Remarks 1-4; Remark 4 truncated mid-definition of the lightlike relation). Body proof not audited. Used as recorded context, not re-derived.
locator: Abstract: 'Causality is represented by a partial ordering on Minkowski space, and the group of all automorphisms that preserve this partial ordering is shown to be generated by the inhomogeneous Lorentz group and dilatations.' Definition: Q(x) = x0^2 - x1^2 - x2^2 - x3^2; x < y if an event at x can influence an event at y; G generated by (i) orthochronous Lorentz (preserve Q and time orientation, possibly reverse space orientation), (ii) translations, (iii) dilations. Remark 2: the result 'depends essentially upon space being more than 1-dimensional'; in 1 space dimension 'the causality group would be much larger than G, and the general causal automorphism would map the space and time axes into curved lines'
assumptions: Minkowski space R^4; causality as strict partial order; order-preserving bijections
conclusion: Causality group = G as defined (inhomogeneous Lorentz group plus dilations, with space reversal allowed); dimension >= 2 space essential
proof_status: Statement and remarks read; proof body not audited this run
open_questions: Alexandrov/Zeeman generalization to arbitrary dimension n >= 3 not checked this run
Exact extent of Aut(M, <<) in 1+1 not needed and not determined

title: A Syntactic Characterization of Morita Equivalence
relevance: Exact scope hypothesis for any 'category equivalence = Morita equivalence' identification (RESULT.md 5.3): Morita equivalence in the sense of Johnstone (equivalent categories of models naturally in any Grothendieck topos) equals Barrett-Halvorson common definitional extension, for cartesian, regular, coherent, geometric AND first-order theories
limits: Abstract read on the arXiv page (v1, 8 Jul 2015). Body theorem not audited; JSL version (DOI 10.1017/jsl.2017.59, inherited from the predecessor record) not opened.
exact_version: arXiv:1507.02302v1 (8 Jul 2015); Journal of Symbolic Logic (2017), DOI 10.1017/jsl.2017.59 (inherited metadata)
locator: Abstract verbatim: 'We characterize Morita equivalence of theories in the sense of Johnstone in terms of a new syntactic notion of a common definitional extension developed by Barrett and Halvorson for cartesian, regular, coherent, geometric and first-order theories. This provides a purely syntactic characterization of the relation between two theories that have equivalent categories of models naturally in any Grothendieck topos.'
assumptions: Doctrines: cartesian, regular, coherent, geometric, first-order; Johnstone-sense Morita equivalence of categories of models in any Grothendieck topos
conclusion: Authors' claim: within that scope, Morita equivalence = common definitional extension
open_questions: Whether single-sorted first-order theories fall under the needed doctrine formulation - check in body before any use
